q: 1. In which year the term 'Sustainable Development' came into existence?
explain: The term was first introduced in the World Conservation Strategy (WCS) in 1980, though it was later popularized by the Brundtland Report in 1987.

q: 2. Which famous report on sustainable development was titled 'Our Common Future'?
explain: The Brundtland Report, published in 1987 by the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED), is formally titled 'Our Common Future'.

q: 3. When was Sustainable Development policy introduced in Nepal?
explain: Nepal formally integrated sustainable development concepts and environmental impact assessments during the 8th Five Year Plan (1992–1997).

q: 4. What is/are core element(s) of Sustainable Development?
explain: Sustainable development is built on three main pillars: economic viability, social equity, and environmental protection.

q: 5. How many Sustainable Development Goals have been set by the United Nations Sustainable Development Summit - 2015?
explain: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all UN Member States in 2015, defines 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

q: 6. Among the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, 13th Goal is
explain: Goal 13 specifically calls for urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.

q: 7. Who was first coined the term "Sustainable Development"?
explain: Barbara Ward is often credited with pioneering the concept in the 1970s, emphasizing the link between economic development and environmental care.

q: 8. Who is the activist who led the 'Chipko Movement' for environmental conservation?
explain: He led this movement around 1973 against deforestation in the Garhwal region of India.

q: 9. Which statement depicts the best definition of sustainable development?
options: It means optimal utilization of natural resources.
Sustainable use of natural resources without considering the need of the future generation
Present generation fulfills its needs while consider the needs of the future generation as well
explain: The classic definition is development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

q: 10. The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development Goals acknowledge that all governments must Promote action in:
options: People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace and Partnership
People, Environment, Prosperity, Peace and Foresight
explain: These are known as the '5 Ps' that inform the SDGs: People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace, and Partnership.

q: 11. Among the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, which of the following goal is not related to with Nepal?
explain: As a landlocked country, Goal 14 (Life Below Water), which focuses on oceans and marine resources, is not directly applicable to Nepal's geography.

q: 12. How many targets have been set by sustainable development goals to eliminate all kinds of poverty and hunger by 2030 A.D.?
explain: The 17 Sustainable Development Goals are accompanied by 169 specific targets to be achieved by 2030.

q: 13. "We don't have plan B because there is no planet B." Whose Statement is this regarding to the development of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)?
explain: This famous quote was delivered by former UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon to emphasize the urgency of climate action.

q: 14. Agenda-21 related --------
explain: Agenda 21 is a non-binding action plan of the United Nations with regard to sustainable development.

q: 15. The first country to sign in Agenda 21 is ---------
explain: China was one of the earliest and most prominent signatories to commit to the implementation of Agenda 21.

q: 16. During which plan period, the Environmental protection act and Rules were enacted and enforced in Nepal?
explain: The Environment Protection Act (2053) and Rules (2054) were enacted during the 8th Plan period in Nepal.

q: 17. Earth watch is related to ----------
explain: Earthwatch Institute is an international non-profit organization that focuses on environmental conservation through scientific field research.

q: 18. The first environment day in Nepal was observed in?
explain: Nepal began celebrating World Environment Day in 1976, following the global trend started in 1974.

q: 19. Which country has been started the movement of "Earth hour"?
explain: Earth Hour started as a lights-off event in Sydney, Australia, in 2007, organized by WWF-Australia.

q: 20. Which of the following is correct slogan regarding International Environment Day - 2025 celebrated on 5th June every year?
options: Save the earth, save our environment
explain: As per the answer key provided in the book, the slogan for 2025 is 'Save the earth, save our environment'.

q: 21. Earth hour 2025 was celebrated throughout the world to combat climate change and protect biodiversity and nature. What edition of 'Earth Hour' was it?
explain: Counting from its inception in 2007, the 2025 event marks the 19th edition of Earth Hour.

q: 22. Which ISO specifies audit protocol of environment?
explain: ISO 14064 provides specifications for the quantification, monitoring, and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and removals.

q: 23. Who is the founder of Green Belt Movement?
explain: The Green Belt Movement was founded by Nobel Laureate Wangari Maathai in Kenya in 1977.

q: 24. Who is awarded WWF Conservation Award 2020 A.D.?
explain: Rinzin Phunjok Lama, a Nepali conservationist, was recognized for his work in the high-altitude Himalayas.

q: 25. Who received Blue Planet Award 2024 A.D.?
explain: Professor Robert Costanza is recognized for his pioneering work in ecological economics.

q: 26. Who was the first Nepali to receive the Global-500 award?
explain: Dr. Krishna Kumar Pandey was the first Nepali to be honored with the UNEP Global 500 award for environmental achievement.

q: 27. Global 500 'awards are given for the outstanding achievement in which of the following fields?
explain: The Global 500 Roll of Honour was a tribute to environmental achievers from around the world.

q: 28. Who published the "Red Data Book" about the list of rare animals?
explain: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) maintains and publishes the Red List of Threatened Species.

q: 29. Organization related to 'Red Data Book' or 'Red List' is -------
explain: As noted in question 36, IUCN is the authority responsible for the Red List.

q: 30. CITES is related to ----------
options: Protection of Endangered species of wild Flora and Fauna
explain: CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora.

q: 31. Which of the following pairs is wrong?
explain: WWF was established in 1961, not 1960, making option (a) the incorrect pair.

q: 32. Which Country is not included in ICIMOD?
explain: The eight member countries of ICIMOD are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, and Pakistan. Thailand is not a member.

q: 33. Which of the following is incorrect?
explain: World Environment Day was established in 1972 but first celebrated in 1974.

q: 34. Sound is said to be hazardous when its Intensity is above ---------
explain: Prolonged exposure to noise levels above 80-85 decibels (dB) can lead to permanent hearing damage.

q: 35. Which one of the following is not a secondary Pollutant?
explain: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) is a primary pollutant because it is emitted directly from a source. The others are formed through chemical reactions in the atmosphere.

q: 36. Kyoto protocol (1997) is related with ----------
options: Reduction of emission of green house gas
explain: The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty that committed state parties to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

q: 37. The concept of 'Carbon credit' originated from:
explain: The Kyoto Protocol introduced the market-based mechanisms of carbon credits to help countries reach emission targets.

q: 38. Which country in the world responsible for largest percentage of global house gas (GHG) emissions?
explain: China is currently the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases due to its large population and industrial base.

q: 39. 'Montreal Protocol' is related to ---------
explain: The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of substances like CFCs.

q: 40. When did Nepal signed Paris Agreement?
explain: Nepal signed the Paris Agreement on the very first day it opened for signature, April 22, 2016.

q: 41. According to IPCC, what part in the world, Nepal contributes greenhouse gas emission?
explain: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), Nepal's share of global greenhouse gas emissions is approximately 0.027%.

q: 42. How long has Nepal declared its commitment to zero emission strategy (Zero Net Strategy) at the Glasgow conference on climate change in 2021?
explain: At COP26 in Glasgow, Nepal committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2045.

q: 43. Who was coined the term Global warming?
explain: Wallace 'Wally' Broecker popularized the term 'Global Warming' in a 1975 scientific paper.

q:
44. Consider the following Statement & Choose the correct one: 
 I. The Earth Summit 1992 issued United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) 
 II. 10-10-10 is related to climate change.
explain: The UNFCCC was a major outcome of the 1992 Earth Summit, and '10-10-10' refers to a global day of climate action held on October 10, 2010.

q: 45. UNFCCC COP -29 conferences, Baku, Azerbaijan focused on ----------
options: The reduction of Green house & its emission
explain: The COP29 summit in Baku is heavily focused on setting a new global goal for climate finance to support developing nations.

q: 46. The one which isn't considered as naturally occurring green house greenhouse gas is --------
explain: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are entirely man-made (synthetic) chemicals and do not occur naturally.

q: 47. Which one of the following pairs of gases are the major causes of "Green House Effect"?
explain: Carbon dioxide (CO2) and Methane (CH4) are the two most significant contributors to the anthropogenic greenhouse effect.

q: 48. Which one of the following is mainly responsible for green house effect?
explain: While many gases contribute, CO2 is the primary driver of climate change due to the sheer volume released by human activity.

q: 49. Which of the following is true for the relative contribution of various Green gases to total Global warming?
explain: The magnitude of contribution generally follows the order: Carbon dioxide > Methane > Nitrous Oxide > CFCs.

q: 50. Which of the following is not a green house gas?
explain: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a direct greenhouse gas, though it can influence the lifetime of other greenhouse gases like methane.
